Package com.lemarketjames.market.model

Class GbmModel

java.lang.Object
com.lemarketjames.market.model.GbmModel
public final class GbmModel extends Object
Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM) price math.

GBM models a price whose log returns are normally distributed: dS = mu * S * dt + sigma * S * dW. We use the exact discrete solution rather than a linear (Euler) approximation, which guarantees prices stay positive and avoids a systematic upward bias: 

   S(t + dt) = S(t) * exp((mu - sigma^2 / 2) * dt + sigma * sqrt(dt) * Z),   Z ~ N(0, 1)

Kept free of Spring and state so the maths can be unit tested in isolation.

  • Method Details

    • nextPrice

      public static double nextPrice(double price, double drift, double volatility, double dtYears, double shock)
      Advances a price by one time step.
      Parameters:
      price - current price, must be positive
      drift - annualised expected return (mu), e.g. 0.08
      volatility - annualised volatility (sigma), e.g. 0.25
      dtYears - length of the step in trading years
      shock - standard normal random draw (Z)
      Returns:
      the next price, always positive

    • correlatedShock

      public static double correlatedShock(double marketShock, double idiosyncraticShock, double marketCorrelation)
      Blends a market-wide shock with an instrument-specific shock using a one-factor model: Z = rho * Z_market + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * Z_own.

      The result is still standard normal, so volatility is unchanged, but instruments with a higher rho move together more often, as real stocks do on market-wide news.

      Parameters:
      marketShock - shared standard normal draw for this tick
      idiosyncraticShock - instrument's own standard normal draw
      marketCorrelation - rho in [0, 1]
      Returns:
      the correlated standard normal shock
